sections.label: Design 2025 master plan
sections.summary: The Design 2025 master plan was developed last year in recognition of this.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Recognising this, the Design 2025 master plan was developed last year.

sections.label: Main amendments to design law
sections.summary: The main amendments broaden design protection, change commissioned design ownership, lengthen the grace period, and ease multiple design filings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The main amendments are, first, to broaden the scope of design protection under the Registered Designs Act (RDA); second, to change the default position on ownership of a commissioned design; third, to broaden the scope of, and lengthen, the designs grace period provision; and fourth, to allow multiple designs to be filed in a single application more easily.

sections.label: Commissioned design ownership default
sections.summary: Clauses 3(a) to 3(c) amend legislation so designers are treated as owners of commissioned designs by default.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Clauses 3(a) to 3(c) of the Bill amend the current legislation so that in commissioning situations, the designer will be treated as the owner of the design by default.

sections.label: Six-month grace period feedback
sections.summary: The six-month grace period is so called, and industry feedback says the current provision should not be so restrictive.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This six-month period is commonly referred to as the "grace period".

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We have received feedback from the industry that the current grace period provision should not be so restrictive.

sections.label: Extending the designs grace period
sections.summary: Clause 7 inserts section 8A, extending the grace period from six to 12 months and covering disclosures originating from the designer.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To this end, clause 7 of the Bill inserts a new section 8A, which will give designers greater flexibility by extending the grace period from six months to 12 months, and expanding the situations under which the grace period provision may be relied upon to include any disclosure originating from the designer.

sections.label: Multiple designs in one application
sections.summary: Clause 10(b) amends section 11 of the RDA to enable multiple designs in a single application, subject to requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Clause 10(b) amends section 11 of RDA to enable multiple designs to be filed in a single application, subject to certain requirements.

sections.label: Copyright Act amendments for designs
sections.summary: Clause 28 amends Copyright Act sections 7, 70, 73 and 74 to account for design protection of non-physical products under RDA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As we will now allow the registration of designs of non-physical products under RDA, these provisions in the Copyright Act have to be amended to take into account design protection for non-physical products.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This is effected by clause 28 of the Bill which amends sections 7, 70, 73 and 74 of the Copyright Act.

sections.label: Broadened scope and reduced registration burden
sections.summary: The scope of registrable designs is broadened, designers become recognised owners instead of commissioners, and registration cost and burden are reduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, the scope of registrable designs under the Act has been broadened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, the designer of the registrable design is now the recognised owner instead of the commissioner of the work; and third, the administrative burden and cost of registration will be reduced.

sections.label: Micro-SMEs in design survey
sections.summary: The 2014 National Design Industry Survey found that 86% of Singapore design firms were micro-SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In the 2014 National Design Industry Survey, it was found that 86% of design firms in Singapore were micro-SMEs.

sections.label: Low awareness of design rights
sections.summary: Only 818 of 4,268 designs filed at IPOS in 2014 were by local applicants, and awareness of design rights appeared low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: While efforts have been made to widen the scope of protection under the Bill and to increase access to protection of designs, these efforts will come to naught if the public lacks awareness of these rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: It is notable that out of a total of 4,268 designs filed at the IP Office of Singapore (IPOS) in 2014, only 818 are designs filed by Singapore-based or local applicants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In the review of the Act conducted by MinLaw and IPOS, it was found that the level of awareness on the use and enforcement of design rights in Singapore appeared to be low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: With the passing of the Bill, education and outreach efforts need to be made to raise awareness of design rights and address overlaps of copyright and trademark protection with the registered designs regime.

sections.label: High Court infringement action costs
sections.summary: Infringement actions must be commenced in the High Court, which may be too costly for small businesses and freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Under the Act, infringement actions must be commenced in the High Court and such legal action may be too costly for small businesses and freelancers to pursue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: It is also timely to consider whether a simpler and less costly adjudication regime can be made available to smaller players to protect their registered rights.

sections.label: Matching EU design standards
sections.summary: Extending the grace period to 12 months, recognising colour, and clarifying designer ownership are examples of matching EU standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, extending the grace period from six months to 12 months matches that of the EU.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Recognising colour as a protectable design feature and clarifying that ownership rests in designers rather than the commissioning parties are other examples of matching EU standards.

sections.label: Law students on design overlap
sections.summary: The IP Students' Association raised concern that non-physical products under RDA could overlap with patent law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The IP Students' Association, comprising law students in both the National University of Singapore (NUS) and the Singapore Management University (SMU), also raised the concern that non-physical products under RDA could lead to some overlap with patent law, since the line between the design and the function of a non-physical product is less clear.

sections.label: IPOS guidance notes on interface
sections.summary: IPOS will explore issuing guidance notes to address knowledge gaps such as the interface between registered design and copyright protection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In addition to these collaborations, IPOS will explore issuing guidance notes to address specific knowledge gaps, for example, the interface between registered design protection and copyright protection.

sections.label: Committee reviewing IP dispute resolution
sections.summary: MinLaw appointed a Committee to review Singapore's IP dispute resolution system, which recommended reducing enforcement costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This is something that MinLaw is looking into.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We had appointed a Committee, comprising representatives from the judiciary, the IP Bar, academia, IP-rich companies and Government agencies to review the IP dispute resolution system in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Committee has made recommendations on how enforcement costs can be reduced.
